claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxygen uptake during high-temperature exposure in air.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr suffers pesting during high-temperature exposure in air.
A dilute yttrium-containing slurry followed by inert-atmosphere heat treatment at 800 °C for 1 hour will induce yttrium segregation to the alloy surface.
The treatment will produce a yttrium-enriched surface layer.
The yttrium-enriched surface layer will cause the oxide scale to incorporate Y2O3 particles.
Incorporation of Y2O3 particles will enhance oxide-scale adhesion.
Incorporation of Y2O3 particles will reduce oxide-scale spallation.
Yttrium will segregate to the metal–oxide interface during oxidation.
Interfacial yttrium segregation will slow oxide-growth kinetics.
Interfacial yttrium segregation will limit oxygen ingress.
The surface treatment will leave the bulk alloy microstructure unchanged.
Leaving the bulk microstructure unchanged will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated material, Y-treated HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit a significantly slower oxide-growth rate in air at 800 °C for up to 5 hours.
Relative to untreated material, Y-treated HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit diminished pesting in air at 800 °C for up to 5 hours.
After treatment, the alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
After treatment, the alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The exposure and loading boundary is specified at 800 °C, while the claimed retained yield strength is defined at 1000 °C; the experiment does not clearly specify a separate post-exposure 1000 °C strength test capable of evaluating that prediction.
